• Work only on a fully disassembled, unloaded firearm (slide, barrel, recoil spring removed).

• Observe all federal, state and local laws (ATF rules, hazardous-waste disposal, VOC limits, FFL requirements where applicable).

1. Cerakote® or other ceramic-polymer coatings  
   – Tools & materials:  
     • Air-abrasive (bead) blaster with aluminum oxide media  
     • HVLP spray gun or airbrush compatible with Cerakote  
     • Dedicated curing oven (maintains 200 °F–300 °F uniformly)  
     • 3M high-temp masking tape and silicone plugs  
   – Safety:  
     • NIOSH-approved organic-vapor respirator, nitrile gloves, eye protection  
     • Shop ventilation rated for isocyanates/VOCs  
   – Steps:  
     1. Abrasive-blast all metal and polymer surfaces evenly to 220–320 grit profile.  
     2. Clean with acetone or brake-cleaner; let dry.  
     3. Mask off firing-control areas (slide rails, breech face, sights).  
     4. Apply thin, even Cerakote coats per manufacturer’s flash-time guidelines.  
     5. Cure in oven at specified temp/time.  
   – Compliance: follow local EPA VOC rules; waste disposal per MSDS.

2. Hydrographic (“water transfer”) dipping  
   – Tools & materials:  
     • Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) barrier film and printed graphics film  
     • Hydro dip tank with heater (maintained at 80 °F–90 °F)  
     • Activator spray, primer (EP or urethane), clear topcoat  
     • Standard gunsmith bench vise with protective jaws  
   – Safety:  
     • Chemical-resistant gloves, face shield, apron  
     • Fume extraction for primer/topcoat  
   – Steps:  
     1. Prime surfaces with adhesion primer; let cure.  
     2. Base-coat in your chosen background color; dry fully.  
     3. Float PVA film in water, spray activator, then lay printed film on top.  
     4. Slowly dip slide/frame at 30°–40° angle for even wrap.  
     5. Rinse off residue, let dry, then apply clear topcoat (2K urethane preferred).  
   – Compliance: ensure disposal of rinse water and paint sludge per local hazardous-waste rules.

3. Laser marking/engraving  
   – Tools & materials:  
     • Fiber-laser or diode-laser engraving system (10–30 W) with fixture  
     • CAD/vector software for artwork  
     • Fume extractor with carbon filter  
   – Safety:  
     • ANSI Z136.1 laser-safety goggles matched to wavelength  
     • Enclosed housing with interlocks or beam curtain  
   – Steps:  
     1. Mount slide/frame in a rigid, non-reflective fixture.  
     2. Align focal distance; run low-power test marks off-zone.  
     3. Engrave serial-compliance text, logos or patterns at safe depth (≤0.1 mm).  
     4. Lightly clean residue with isopropyl alcohol.  
   – Compliance: do not obliterate legally required markings; respect copyright on artwork.

4. PVD/TiN or DLC coatings  
   – Tools & materials:  
     • Professional PVD vacuum chamber (for TiN, CrN) or DLC plasma system

     • Follow chemical handling protocols for precursor gases (titanium chloride, methane)

     1. Degrease parts ultrasonically; bake-out moisture.  
     2. Mask zones (sights, internals).  
     3. Run PVD cycle: base pressure, gas introduction, target sputtering, deposition.  
     4. Vent chamber, de-mask, inspect adhesion (tape pull test).  
   – Compliance: permit for vacuum-deposition facility; chemical-waste disposal per EPA.

5. Custom grip stippling or slide checkering  
   – Tools & materials:  
     • Temperature-controlled soldering iron or rotary tool with carbide/cross-cut bits  
     • Fine needle files, brass-wire brush for blending  
   – Safety:  
     • Heat-resistant gloves, eye protection, respirator for polymer dust  
     • Work on a heat-resistant bench pad  
   – Steps:  
     1. Mark layout lines for grip panels or slide serrations.  
     2. Heat-stippling tool to ~600 °F; practice on scrap polymer.  
     3. Create consistent dot pattern on frame; avoid over-penetration.  
     4. Final-blend edges with files to remove sharp burrs.  
   – Compliance: ensure no contact with trigger mechanism or frame rails; preserved safety margins.
